principles.statement: Failure states are named, persisted, and bounded: interrupted is not completed, failed_after_max_attempts is not retried forever, discarded is not accepted.
principles.rationale: Live-verified across the whole system: boot reconciliation marks stranded tasks interrupted; the meta-loop's 10-attempt cap writes outcome=failed_after_max_attempts; shell drafts are logged as discarded with the reason; rollback reports what it threw away.

principles.statement: Never fabricate success to close a loop: a discard is a discard, a skip is a skip, and an honest failure is a valid terminal state.
principles.rationale: Placeholder drafts are discarded rather than persisted, gaps stay open rather than being covered by shells, and rate-limited attempts are counted as attempts — the system never manufactures a green check.

principles.statement: Restart reconciliation is part of the failure contract: whatever a crash strands must be found, named, and honestly re-queued or marked.
principles.rationale: Boot reconciliation interrupted stranded tasks; AMT islands and gap queues survived crashes intact because their state is durable first and in-memory only second.

heuristics.name: Writing any loop, queue, or workflow state machine.
heuristics.description: Every terminal state has a name, a persisted marker, and a bounded path to reach it; nothing times out into ambiguity.
heuristics.when_to_apply: All background loops and task flows.

heuristics.name: Handling a flaky dependency (LLM APIs, rate limits, local models).
heuristics.description: Count the attempt, escalate through real fallbacks, cap honestly, and record the outcome — the count and the cap are the honesty contract.

decision_rules.condition: A run ends without its goal.
decision_rules.action: Mark the durable state with the named failure outcome and the reason; the next pass decides from that record, never from silence.
